title: [Bug] Subagent spawning fails with "inherit" model when using subagent_type from agent files
body:
**Bug Description**
My spawned team members from existing agents (e.g. `subagent_type: product-owner`, uses  ~/.claude/agents/product-owner.md) are throwing `There's an issue with the selected model (inherit). It may not exist or you may not have access to it. Run /model to pick a different model.`. If they are spawned without the `subagent_type` value, they are `general-purpose` agents and seem to work fine. See chat for details from lead agent's debugging efforts.


**Chat Transcript**

⏺ All three agents delivered. Shutting down and cleaning up.

⏺ They're not responding to shutdowns — just force-cleaning up.

⏺ Bash(rm -rf ~/.claude/teams/product-spec-m4n8 ~/.claude/tasks/product-spec-m4n8)
  ⎿  Done

⏺ Done. Stopped.

  ---
  What we learned from this run:

  The subagent_type: product-owner agents were completely broken as teammates — even after removing the tool restriction from the definition file, they never responded. Switching to general-purpose
  agents with the role described in the prompt worked exactly like the comedy duo: all three delivered their full outputs via SendMessage.

  The root finding: the subagent_type parameter, not just the tools list in the markdown file, is what ultimately determines tool availability for custom agent types. Removing tools: from the file may
  not be sufficient — the agent type itself may have tool restrictions baked in at a deeper level. Using general-purpose (or omitting subagent_type) is the reliable path for agents that need to
  participate in team communication.

❯ USER: When you launch the 3 agents that were successful was that using the `TeamCreate` tool?                                                                                                                

⏺ Yes — TeamCreate was used for all three attempts, including the successful one. The difference wasn't whether TeamCreate was used, but what subagent_type was passed to the Agent tool when spawning
  teammates:

  - Failed runs: subagent_type: product-owner → custom agent type, broken tool access
  - Successful run: subagent_type omitted → defaults to general-purpose → all tools available including SendMessage

  TeamCreate itself worked fine every time. The problem was entirely in how the agents were spawned into the team.

❯ USER:  do you understand what is happening behind The scenes when you set the subagent_type to product-owner ?                                                                                                

⏺ Partially — here's what I know and where I'm uncertain.                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                          
  What I know happens:                                                                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                                       
  When you pass subagent_type: product-owner to the Agent tool, Claude Code looks up ~/.claude/agents/product-owner.md, reads the frontmatter, and uses it to configure the spawned agent:               
  - model: sets the model (or inherits)                                                                                                                                                                  
  - color: sets the UI color                                                                                                                                                                             
  - tools: (when present) hard-restricts which tools the agent gets — this is enforced by the framework, not just advisory
  - The body of the file becomes the agent's system prompt

  What I'm uncertain about:

  Whether the agent definition is r
author: Seth-Green-WWT
